correctness.rationale: The scalar autonomous flow F_t is strictly increasing. Independently rederived for f(x)=x(x−a)(1−x): sign F_t″(x) equals sign[2(1+a)−3(x+F_t(x))] times positive r ∫_0^t F_s′(x) ds. Since x+F_t(x) increases strictly from 0 to 2, F_t′ has a unique maximum. Therefore the fixed-width increment D(x)=F_t(x+q)−F_t(x) is strictly unimodal. Its value relative to q is strictly negative at 0 and 1−q but strictly positive at a−q and a, proving exactly two simple roots with positions as stated. The inverse-flow argument confines the upper root below F_t^{-1}(1−q). Uniform short-time Taylor expansion gives an explicit quadratic with two distinct interior roots; limits of bistable flow yield large-time a−q and a. Independent exact polynomial identity and closed-form a=1/2 example roots 0.14502970560661888 and 0.6549702943933814 reproduced. No conclusion for q outside the stated strict range.
risks: The short-time roots depend on cubic structure; mere order-preservation does not prove unimodality.
The theorem compares two fixed pulse times only, not an optimal continuous release schedule.
